newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi says would quit if Italy misses EMU - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says would quit if Italy misses EMU - magazine.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he would step down if his nation fails to meet the strict requirements for European monetary union, the German business weekly Wirtschaftswoche said on Wednesday.
But Prodi insisted Italy would qualify next year to become a founding member of EMU in 1999.
"I have linked my fate to the Euro," Prodi told the magazine when asked, in an interview to appear on Thursday, if a failure to qualify for EMU would trigger his resignation.
The prime minister also rejected speculation Italy would reach the required level for the budget deficits in 1997 only to overshoot targets in subsequent years.
"I would like to point out that our economic data are closing in on the criteria, while Germany's are moving away," he said. "We will do it, of that I am convinced. We are pushing the tempo."

The Maastricht Treaty requires countries to reduce government debt to 60 percent of gross domestic product and budget deficits to three percent of GDP by next year to qualify for EMU, but allows some flexibility on interpretation.
Prodi also said that Europe could see a return of nationalism if currency union fails.
"The uncertainty about EMU is a disaster for all European nations," he said.
"We must complete the currency union quickly, or the ghosts of once-dead nationalism will awake again. We fear that the political tensions in Europe would break out again."
"That is why, despite all the social and economic problems, the political situation for fulfilling European unity is favorable right now," Prodi said.
